## LYME DISEASE PROPHYLAXIS
## Inpatient/Outpatient/ER Patients who have been bitten while in endemic areas of New England, Mid-
Atlantic States, Minnesota, and Wisconsin where local rate of Ixodes spp. tick
infection rate with Borrelia burgdorferi in an endemic area may be treated with
prophylactic antibiotics for prevention of Lyme disease. Using a wait and see
method by monitoring for signs and symptoms of Lyme disease is also an
acceptable approach in patients who have been bitten by an Ixodes spp. tick.
## All following criteria must be met to be considered for prophylactic treatment
1. Doxycycline is not contraindicated (i.e. allergy, pregnant, lactating)
2. Attached tick is reliably identified as an adult or nymphal Ixodes spp.
Ixodes spp. identification
3. Tick is attached for greater than or equal to 36 hours based on degree of
tick engorgement with blood or likely time of exposure to tick infested area.
4. Prophylaxis must be started within 72 hours after time tick was removed.
5. Bite occurs in a highly endemic area.
CDC Lyme Disease Case Map
## Prophylactic treatment if all of the above criteria are met
Doxycycline PO 200mg once ($) [DI]
